To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Factor graph message passing is a powerful paradigm for automated inference in Bayesian signal processing algorithms and ForneyLab is a promising tool for this purpose.”

(1) ForneyLab enables automated design of Bayesian signal processing and machine learning algorithms, (2) ForneyLab can be used to efficiently implement Bayesian signal processing algorithms for parameter estimation, and (3) ForneyLab appears more efficient and stable than state-of-the-art probabilistic programming frameworks for inference in state-space and other dynamic models.

(1) message passing in Fornye-style factor graphs is a powerful framework for Bayesian inference, (2) the Julia programming language is a good choice for implementing such a framework, (3) the ForneyLab toolbox is a promising tool for automated inference in FFG-based models, (4) variational inference is a good approximation method for inference in FFG models, and (5) variational message passing outperforms ADVI for inference in FSG models.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel probabilistic programming framework for automated design of Bayesian signal processing methods, which we believe will enable a new generation of efficient, flexible and robust algorithms for inference and learning in signal processing and beyond.
the development of a new tool for automated inference in Bayesian signal processing algorithms and the exploration of its capabilities in the design of Bayesian signal processing applications.
the development of a new probabilistic programming paradigm and its application to automated inference in state-of-the-art Bayesian signal processing algorithms.

the FFG framework is a viable alternative to the state of the art probabilistic programming frameworks.

message passing-based FFGs are a powerful framework for Bayesian inference, and that ForneyLab is a promising tool for automated inference in FFG-based models.
